fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Access Drive; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Open Lawn Area; Dense Vegetation; Detached Structure; Patio Area; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Rear Access; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance that is visible from both directions on the road.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow fire apparatus to reach the residence.
• Install a reflective marker or sign identifying the detached structure to help responders locate it quickly on arrival.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clearance for emergency vehicles on both sides and overhead.
• Clear a turnaround area near the residence or detached structure large enough for emergency vehicles to reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Cut back dense vegetation that directly contacts or overhangs the main residence and detached structure.
• Keep a gate or opening in the perimeter fencing accessible from the front to allow responders to reach the rear of the property on foot.
• If a rear gate exists, keep it unlocked or secured with a lock compatible with a standard responder key.
• Mark any pedestrian access points through the perimeter fencing so responders can locate them quickly.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Shrubs; Large Trees; Limited Vegetation Separation; Scattered Trees; Open Terrain; Vegetation Along Driveway; Mixed Vegetation; Ground Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches from trees along the driveway that hang over or close to the travel surface to keep the route clear for vehicles.

• Thin the tree cluster nearest the structure to create open space between the trees and the building.

• Remove or cut back shrubs and low plants that are directly against or touching the structure.

• Separate ground vegetation from the base of the structure by clearing a bare or low-grass band around the building.

• Trim low branches on large trees near the structure so flames cannot climb from ground vegetation up into the tree canopy.

• Thin scattered shrubs and mixed vegetation between the tree clusters and the structure to reduce the amount of connected plant material leading toward the building.

• Keep ground vegetation mowed short in open areas between the structure and surrounding trees and shrubs.
